requirement: Choose exactly one of Option 1 (bounded prompt/schema adjustment), Option 2 (two-pass inventory->composition), Option 3 (three-stage inventory->composition->reconciliation), Option 4 (IR gap, architecture decision required before implementation). Pick the smallest architecture supported by evidence.

eliminationOfOptions.option4_irGapRequiresRedesign: ELIMINATED - 02's own family audit found zero IR_GAP families across all 11 named semantic categories (9 REPRESENTABLE_NOW, 2 PARTIALLY_REPRESENTABLE-but-untested, 0 architecturally deficient). B4's real holdout output is direct empirical proof the IR already handles a genuinely complex, multi-threshold, cure-mechanic covenant end to end.
eliminationOfOptions.option3_threeStageInventoryComposeReconc: ELIMINATED - this is a large, invasive architecture change (a new AI-facing wire schema, a new deterministic reconciliation pass, a new frozen-inventory intermediate state) that the evidence does not support needing. The mission's own central hypothesis motivating this option (Section 2: the model is asked to perform too many semantic operations in one pass, causing dropped/omitted material under high cardinality) is DIRECTLY REFUTED by 01's own A2 finding: the model individually, correctly, precisely reasoned about and dispositioned 19 separate leaf-level clauses in a SINGLE pass with zero evidence of dropping, summarizing, or truncating under load. If cardinality-driven omission is not the real failure mechanism, the architecture designed to fix it is not the right fix.
eliminationOfOptions.option2_twoPassInventoryComposition: ELIMINATED for the same reason as Option 3, at smaller scale - still predicated on a decomposition-capacity problem that 01's evidence does not support. A lighter two-pass split would add real implementation cost (a new inventory wire schema, a new consistency layer between passes, new failure modes at the pass boundary) to solve a problem the evidence shows is not occurring.

whyOption1.summary: 01's own per-claim analysis found exactly ONE concrete, generalizable, evidence-supported architectural defect across all 7 residual failing claims: checkIntraDefinitionComponentCompleteness (added in the immediately preceding session) does not recurse into a nested UNSUPPORTED node's own attemptedStructure, so it dramatically undercounts how much of a DEEPLY NESTED composite tree (B2's 8-level IF chain) actually survived normalization - reporting 2/4 components when the true, manually-confirmed count is roughly 36/38. This is a bounded, single-function, diagnostic-layer fix, squarely within Option 1's own 'bounded prompt/tool-schema adjustment' scope generalized to include a bounded, generic, evidence-driven refinement within the existing single-pass architecture (the SAME class of fix as the immediately preceding session's own buildComposite change - both are about NOT LOSING VISIBILITY into structure that was actually built, never about restructuring how the model is asked to work).
whyOption1.remainingFindings: The other 6 claims (A1, B3: genuine source-context truncation, out of decomposition-architecture scope; A5, B2's two real leaves: genuine, narrow condition-type representability gaps for context-dependent branching and discretionary elections, real but too narrow to justify a general architecture redesign; A2: not a defect; B1, B4: verifier-side semantic-accuracy concerns, a different subsystem) require no architecture change at all - they are either out of scope, already-correctly-flagged real gaps, or non-defects.

additionalBoundedConsideration.item: A2/A5's real, narrow leaf-level representability gaps (a discretionary-election condition; a context-dependent/usage-branching condition slot) are noted but NOT implemented as new IR node kinds this session - per the mission's own 'do not introduce schema migration unless truly unavoidable' discipline (carried forward from the prior session), and because each affects exactly one leaf in one real claim, not a systemic pattern across the whole-agreement family audit (02). Recorded here as a disclosed, deferred, out-of-scope residual for a future session, not silently worked around.

conclusion: Implement the bounded completeness-check.ts recursive-descent fix (Section 5/17's own requirement) as this mission's sole production code change to the semantic-computation layer, plus the whole-agreement-general synthetic test corpus (Section 8) to validate the fix and the family audit's REPRESENTABLE_NOW claims empirically, before proceeding to production freeze and the frozen-holdout/whole-agreement reality-check gates.
